item.title: Norris demands ban for Colapinto after Azerbaijan GP crash
item.content:encoded: Reigning world champion Lando Norris thinks Franco Colapinto deserves "at least a one-race ban" for causing a pile-up at Formula 1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.On a lap 36 restart in the streets of Baku, Colapinto locked up his cold front tyres and aimlessly speared into Alpine team-mate Gasly into Turn 1, with Norris also collected by the tangling pair.The incident knocked both Gasly and ...Keep reading

item.title: Norris wants F1 race ban for Colapinto
item.author: Valentin Khorounzhiy
item.content:encoded: Lando Norris says Franco Colapinto should face a Formula 1 race ban for his error during the Azerbaijan Grand Prix that took Norris, Colapinto and Pierre Gasly out of the race.After a fairly processional first 30-plus laps of the Baku race, Colapinto had a massive lock-up while entering Turn 1 on a safety car restart while running in 10th place, seemingly caught out by the rate of deceleration from the Mercedes of Kimi Antonelli ahead of him.He avoided hitting Antonelli but instead had to hug the inside wall and never scrubbed off anywhere near enough speed, ploughing into Alpine team-mate Gasly in the braking zone, with the chain reaction also eliminating Norris.It was an error that Norris, who had had a particularly difficult weekend up to then and had his own Turn 1 mistake just before the safety car, did not take kindly to.Norris stressed that he had not seen the replay at the time of speaking but said: "I think the FIA should be more strict and start handing out bans for this kind of stuff. It's just careless from people."It costs a lot of money, all my parts are in the bin now. People should just get banned, because that's not driving that deserves to be in Formula 1."On whether race leader George Russell's approach to the restart bunched up the field too much, he said: "George can do what he wants."In Formula 1 I think you expect drivers to anticipate things, know grip is going to be low, know tyre temps are low - they weren't even that low."In Formula 1 you want to be against the best drivers in the world, and when stuff like this happens, it's because...yeah, [it] shouldn't be there."He reiterated later that he wanted "at least a one-race ban" for this kind of crash.A race ban in F1 requires a driver to amass 12 penalty points in a 12-month period - which has become a lot less likely since the FIA revised its approach to penalty points, seeking only to penalise what it perceived as actively dangerous driving or unsportsmanlike conduct.By virtue of a number of yellow flag infringements, Colapinto is joint-top with Carlos Sainz in the current penalty points leaderboard - but, pending a verdict on this incident, that still means only four points, so there is no precedent under the current system by which he would be banned for the next round.Colapinto, for his part, was immediately apologetic on the radio and maintained that tone in his media appearance."I was out of control completely. Not a lot more to say than sorry to the team, to Pierre, of course, to all the factory," he said."I'm sorry to Lando also. I'm sorry to everyone. It was a big mistake, of course."He didn't respond specifically to Norris's suggestion of a race ban but said: "I do expect to get something [in terms of a penalty], of course. I don't know, I'm not a steward."A 10-second penalty was assessed against Colapinto as the Baku race concluded - but as he did not reach the finish, this is now set to be converted to a grid drop.

item.title: Russell wins despite late Verstappen challenge
item.content:encoded: Mercedes' George Russell holds off a late challenge from Red Bull's Max Verstappen to win an Azerbaijan Grand Prix enlivened by two late safety car periods.

item.title: Russell denies Verstappen in Azerbaijan GP punctuated by two safety cars
item.author: Jack Benyon
item.content:encoded: George Russell ended a barren run without a Formula 1 victory in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix by just 0.196s over Max Verstappen, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli recovering to fifth from 16th in part thanks to a pair of safety cars for crashes.Russell did everything a leader on a street circuit with a long straight on it should do: he got a good start, immediately cleared the one-second overtake window, and had extended his lead to 12 seconds by the time of the first pit stops.His biggest early cause for concern was "nibbling" the wall at the exit of Turn 15 on lap 25 of 51, but he otherwise ran untroubled until Alex Albon crashing at Turn 4 on lap 31 erased his advantage.The safety car benefitted Russell's team-mate Kimi Antonelli most.Championship leader Antonelli started 16th and actually lost a spot at the start, then took 17 laps to pass seven cars and make it to the points-paying positions. While his progress wasn't as rapid as his comeback win at Monza from 19th, it was risk-averse and steadier with the championship lead likely in mind.He caught and passed Franco Colapinto after erasing a just under four-second gap for ninth and then was gifted eighth when Lando Norris's disappointing race continued as the McLaren driver went straight on with a lock-up at Turn 1.At the point of the safety car Antonelli was eighth and 35s off Russell, but the safety car bunched the field to give him a better chance of progressing and allowed him to switch to the favoured soft tyre.He immediately made up a place on the restart as a massive melee broke out at Turn 1.A massive, near-comical lock-up from Colapinto smashed him into Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly - who'd been seventh on the restart - and also took Norris out, while Liam Lawson was also spun in the concertina effect behind by Arvid Lindblad. "I love getting taken out by my team-mate," said a sarcastic Lawson, while Alpine lost a double-points finish in the chaos - much to Gasly's displeasure and Colapinto's apologies.In the highest-pressure scenario of having Verstappen behind, Russell absolutely nailed the restart on lap 39 but Verstappen remained in overtake mode range until three laps later, and then Verstappen set the fastest lap of the race to close back in - refusing to accept defeat.All the way until two laps to go Verstappen stayed within range and subjected Russell to pressure, until Russell finally built a 1.4s gap, but then Verstappen closed back in on the run to finish line on the final lap once both had cleared the scene of Valtteri Bottas's crashed Cadillac.But Russell was just able to hold on for his first win since the Austria GP in late-June."After the double-yellow I had no boost, had no power," said Russell after the race.Verstappen charged through the field from his eighth-place starting spot in the early stages, and despite some bickering between himself and his engineer over the mediums, and intense early pressure from Isack Hadjar, drove a fine race to take second. He'd passed Oscar Piastri for second already after the first safety car restart.Hadjar bagged an amazing result to take third after three races out injured, and was clearly faster in the early stages and played a great team-mate race by offering to stay behind Verstappen.Fourth-place finisher Charles Leclerc was passed by both the Red Bulls and appeared to struggle for pace, making a podium unlikely on the day, and it could have been worse had Piastri hadn't taken himself out of the battle with a lock-up at the first corner that sent him into the runoff area, compounding McLaren's disappointing day.Antonelli received damage to his floor after being clipped by Ollie Bearman on the first safety car restart, and initially struggled to clear Lewis Hamilton, but finally got past five laps after the second restart at Turn 1 and went no further, taking fifth in another comeback drive.Hamilton was the only driver in the top 10 other than Russell to finish where he started, perhaps reflecting Ferrari's race pace struggles.Behind him, the Alpine-induced crash created chaos and brought a host of cars well out of points contention into play.In-the-news Esteban Ocon may be losing his Haas seat but vaulted team-mate Bearman between the two safety cars, but then was bested on the last lap by just 0.030s - with Lindblad stealing the spot at the line. He avoided a penalty for the Lawson incident and made some opportunistic overtakes to make the best of a tough weekend with seventh place.Ocon took eighth ahead of Bearman, while the upgraded Williams bagged a point through Carlos Sainz, who was as low as 19th after his early stop.Hulkenberg missed out on the point with 11th, ahead of Lawson, Gabriel Bortoleto, Piastri and Sergio Perez.Azerbaijan Grand Prix race result1 George Russell (Mercedes) 51 laps2 Max Verstappen (Red Bull) +0.196s3 Isack Hadjar (Red Bull) +10.704s4 Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) +14.136s5 Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) +15.512s6 Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) +22.382s7 Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) +31.159s8 Esteban Ocon (Haas) +31.189s9 Ollie Bearman (Haas) +31.929s10 Carlos Sainz (Williams) +32.416s11 Nico Hulkenberg (Audi) +33.231s12 Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls) +34.013s13 Oscar Piastri (McLaren) +36.401s14 Sergio Perez (Cadillac) +41.400s15 Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi)* +44.230s16 Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac) +1 lap - accidentDNF Franco Colapinto (Alpine)DNF Pierre Gasly (Alpine)DNF Lando Norris (McLaren)DNF Alex Albon (Williams)DNF Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)DNF Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)

item.title: Racing defensively not an option for bullish Remco Evenepoel and Wout van Aert in World Championships road race, but it's up to Seixas and France 'to make it a long and tough race'
item.author: kirsten.frattini@futurenet.com (Kirsten Frattini)
item.content:encoded: "What mistake will I find hard to forgive myself for if I didn't become world champion on Sunday? That I raced defensively," Remco Evenepoel told in a press conference held at their national team's residence at the Hôtel Mortagne on Friday evening.Evenepoel and Van Aert are just two of several favourites heading into the elite men's 273.7km that includes 3,800m of elevation gain across 12 laps of the Mount Royal circuit and the Camillien-Houde climb (2.3km at 6.2%).Only the strongest riders will survive this race of attrition, with noted rivals including Paul Seixas (France), Mathieu van der Poel (Netherlands), Tom Pidcock (Great Britain) and Isaac del Toro (Mexico), who won on this circuit just two weeks ago at the Grand Prix de Montreal.Evenepoel secured his fourth elite time trial world title last weekend and arrived in Montreal having taken victories at the Clasica San Sebastian and Grand Prix de Quebec; he was also second overall at the Tour de France this year behind five-time winner Tadej Pogačar (Slovenia).Pogačar will not line up to defend his world title won in Kigali last year, after crashing heavily at the Vuelta a España, and Evenepoel doesn't believe that it is Belgium's responsibility to make the race difficult."It is not up to us to do that. Wout van Aert and I are two finishers. Someone like Paul Seixas has to come in alone. Everyone knows that. So the French will have to make it a long and tough race," he said in a interview. "I don't need to be afraid to go to the finish with a group."Even so, Evenepoel said that racing defensively would be his biggest regret.He last won the elite men's road race world title in 2022 in Wollongong, while Van Aert's long list of accomplishments has yet to yield a rainbow jersey on the road.Van Aert comes into this weekend as a favourite after a successful Vuelta a España, where he won two stages, posted eight top-10s, and took the points classification jersey. His biggest win this year, and one of the most memorable, came at Paris-Roubaix, where he hoisted the cobblestone trophy above his head for the first time in his career.A rainbow jersey to match would be a fitting ending to a season of firsts for Van Aert. He reminded the press that he finished second at the Grand Prix de Montreal in 2022 and will understand the circuit's demands. "I don't need to convince anyone, except myself, that this course suits me," he told .Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: Yankees Rivalry Roundup: AL West madness reaches new low
item.author: Andrew Mearns
item.content:encoded: Having moved a scheduled Saturday game against the Orioles up to Friday for a straight doubleheader, the Yankees and O’s split the twin bill. Baltimore blew out Brendan Beck and company in a 10-2 loss in the opener—an ignominious follow-up to CC Sabathia’s number retirement—but Ryan Yarbrough and Will Warren combined to lead them to 17 strikeouts in the 6-3 nightcap win. Most importantly, everyone remained healthy. Wins and losses don’t matter for the regular season at this point! Now, they wait at home for the storm to pass today and see if they can play a Game 162 tomorrow. If not … see you on Tuesday for the Wild Card Series, Boston.Here’s what else was going on Friday among the remaining AL playoff hopefuls.Tampa Bay Rays (97-63) 2, Philadelphia Phillies (87-73) 0We’ll only take a minute on this one since—with all due respect to the playoff hopes of our friends in Philly (but boy is it suddenly getting tense with the Diamondbacks hot on the trail)—it really doesn’t mean much with Tampa Bay locked into the top AL seed. The Phils got a really nice outing from ace Cristopher Sánchez, who fanned 10 Rays in seven innings of work. But he did allow an RBI single to Jonny DeLuca in the first and a solo shot to catcher Nick Fortes in the second, and with the Phillies absolutely sputtering … yeah, that was it. Freddy Peralta blanked Philly through 5.1 before a quartet of relievers completed the four-hit shutout, Bryan Baker notching his 41st save of the season.Boston Red Sox (86-74) 4, Chicago Cubs (88-72) 3 [Game 1]It took a little longer than anyone expected, but the Red Sox officially locked themselves into the No. 5 seed in the American League and a date with the Yankees in the Wild Card Series. The best-of-three will begin on Tuesday with all games in the Bronx. At first, it seemed like Boston’s odd skid would continue when the Cubbies plated three within the first four outs. Tyrone Taylor had doubled in Seiya Suzuki following a one-out walk in the first, and the trio of Matt Shaw, Michael Busch, and No. 9 hitter Miguel Amaya continued the mini-parade against Alec Gamboa in the second with with a single and a pair of doubles, Amaya’s going off the Green Monster to drive in a pair.Part of that rally had involved Shaw getting thrown out on a grounder to third though, and Chicago never scored that fourth run. They would rue that result, with typical starter Jake Bennett getting his first relief appearance in anticipation of the Wild Card showdown and throwing 3.2 scoreless. Greg Weissert and Raymond Burgos continued to keep the Cubs off the board for the rest of the game as their offense rallied off Clay Holmes. A rare error by Dansby Swanson brought in the first Boston run in the fourth, and Holmes allowed a leadoff single to former Yankees teammate Isiah Kiner-Falefa in the fifth, followed by a Roman Anthony double. He got one more out, but Caleb Thielbar entered and allowed a game-tying knock from Adley Rutschman.The Red Sox took the lead in the seventh, breaking the tie off Aaron Civale when Anthony tripled and Connor Wong doubled him in. With Weissert and Burgos silencing Chicago, that was all she wrote. The only downside for Boston was that surprise story Mickey Gasper had to leave the game early with biceps discomfort.Boston Red Sox (87-74) 2, Chicago Cubs (88-73) 0 [Game 2]The weather got gloomier as the day went along but the Red Sox left Fenway with a clean doubleheader sweep. Boston kept Brayan Bello in playoff tune-up mode despite coming off an outing of eight innings of 11-K, one-run ball, and they still twirled a shutout. Bello blanked Chicago through four, departed with his pitch count at 58, and gave way to rookie Jedixson Paez, making his fifth career appearance. Paez outpitched Bello, fanning five in five shutout frames to earn his first career win.David Peterson’s own five zeroes for the Cubs were in vain. The scoreless tie was broken up in the eighth with IKF and Jahmai Jones (another former Yankee) on base after walks. Wilyer Abreu cracked a double off Ryan Rolison to plate both runners. That was all Boston needed. The Cubs had hoped to host a Wild Card Series at Wrigley, but that’s looking unlikely now with the Padres a game and a half ahead of them. Game 162 will determine their flight path, and they’ll need a flight just to play it. The nor’easter is not supposed to get any better in Beantown over the weekend, so the Sunday game will be at a neutral site: Tropicana Field. Let’s get weird.Texas Rangers (79-81) 2, Minnesota Twins (76-84) 10When Jacob deGrom was rehabbing from Tommy John surgery, opportunities like this one undoubtedly drove him. Yes, the AL West is lousy, but the Rangers can easily win it and they had deGrom out there against a team playing out the string in the Twins. Even with Joe Ryan on the bump opposing him, they felt great. Instead, Minnesota clobbered deGrom and tallied six in the second, Luke Keaschall delivering the big blow on a two-run triple. The two-time Cy Young Award winner was tagged for eight runs in four innings of work. The news got worse for the Rangers learned that top bat Josh Jung broke his hand on a hit-by-pitch; he’s likely done for 2026. This one had to hurt, and deGrom was furious at himself in the postgame, saying multiple times that he was “embarrassed.”Houston Astros (79-81) 5, The Athletics (64-96) 6Well don’t worry Jacob because remember: the AL West is lousy. The Rangers lost while the Astros were still playing on Friday, so they had a golden opportunity to seize control of the AL West, especially because they own the tiebreaker and were facing a terrible A’s team. Said terrible A’s team held off Houston and won, 6-5. A six-run sixth proved to be enough for the A’s offense as Hunter Brown’s once-solid outing went by the wayside with awful relief from Bennett Sousa, who failed to record a single out and allowed three runs. Henry Bolte smacked a two-run triple in the frame and the A’s had a commanding 6-1 lead. Houston did fight back, in part because the A’s bullpen is horrific. Cam Smith homered and a rally in the eighth broke the score to 6-5 with runners on second and third after a wild pitch. Baby Bomber alum Luis Medina fanned Smith though and Houston was held at bay. Nelson Velázquez got a one-out walk in the ninth to put the go-ahead run on against Hogan Harris, only to be erased on a Jeremy Peña double play ball, stranding Yordan Alvarez in the on-deck circle. For the first time in MLB history, we are guaranteed a full-season division winner with either a .500 record or worse because neither Houston nor Texas can be better than 81-81.Cleveland Guardians (84-76) 12, Kansas City Royals (68-92) 9Funky one in KC. The Guardians maintained their hot streak and withstood rallies from the Royals to win late without actually getting all that many hits. They had a dozen runs scored but only nine hits. Carter Jensen slugged two homers and drove in five for the Royals, but it wasn’t nearly enough, even with a tied-up ballgame at 7-7. walks and a fielder’s choice in the eighth led to Cleveland plating three without a hit before the surging Angel Martinez drove in two with a double to make it a 12-7 game. Salvador Perez’s 324th career homer cut into the lead in the ninth, but the Guardians held on to maintain their one-game lead in the AL Central.Chicago White Sox (83-77) 6, Colorado Rockies (57-103) 1Munetaka Murakami clobbered a pair of dingers to reach 35 in his rookie MLB season, and both came off countryman Tomoyuki Sugano, who he’d homered against twice in NPB play. Sean Burke threw 5.1 innings with one run allowed, and all that was easily plenty for the Pale Hose to take care of business on the South Side. They’ll just need some help from KC if they’re going to pass Cleveland for the division again.

item.title: As it happened: Dutch star secures first road title in illustrious career at World Road Championships women's road race 2026
item.author: Lyne Lamoureux
item.content:encoded: Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia. Subscribers get unlimited access to exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go! Hi. Bonjour. Welcome to our live report on for the elite women's road race on the final weekend of the 2026 UCI World Road Championships in Montréal, Canada.September 26, 2026 – 8:37 AMReigning champion Magdeleine Vallieres of Canada shared her thoughts on social media on the eve of the road race.September 26, 2026 – 8:42 AMWill Dutch racer Demi Vollering finally win a world title today? She lines up as the top favourite, having swept almost all before her this season.September 26, 2026 – 8:52 AMMore on Vollering from Laurens ten Dam, the Dutch team coach: "She is incredibly focused, that's true. Two days after the Tour de France, I got the first message already from her, 'OK, job's not finished'. I was like, 'OK, she's on'," Ten Dam told on Thursday evening.'Job's not finished' – Demi Vollering keeping quiet on game plan as she leads Dutch squad at Road World ChampionshipsTwo-time Tour de France Femmes winner thrives on responsibility this year as lone team leader for first rainbow rewardSeptember 26, 2026 – 8:55 AMAlong with Vallieres, Belgian leader Lotte Kopecky is the only previous World Champion lining up at the start. She won twice before, in Glasgow in 2023 and Zurich in 2024.Speaking on Friday, Kopecky acknowledged that Demi Vollering stands out as the favourite, but said plenty of other contenders are in the mix.'She might well be the woman to beat' – Lotte Kopecky acknowledges Demi Vollering is top World Championships favourite but points to strong field of contenders'If that top day comes, then a lot is possible' says two-time world champion of her own chances in MontrealSeptember 26, 2026 – 8:58 AMThree minutes until the start in Brossard - more on the route coming up.It is sunny in Brossard, with cool temperatures around 12°C, but the day should warm up, as the forecast calls for a high of 23°C in Montréal.September 26, 2026 – 8:59 AMThe 140 riders representing 57 nations, including new countries of Panama, the Philippines and Saudi Arabia are off.They will face 2570 metres of elevation gain over the 180.4km course featuring the closing Mount Royal circuit.September 26, 2026 – 9:08 AMStarting on the South Shore in Brossard, the women head south on an approximately 43km loop through Carignan, Chambly, and Richelieu in the Montérégie region before returning to Brossard and heading to Montréal.The peloton will then ride the Samuel-De Champlain Bridge towards the Mount Royal circuit which the women will tackle eight times, after having 73km in the legs already. The now-iconic circuit features several major challenges: the Voie Camillien-Houde, the Chemin de la Polytechnique, and the tough false flat rising along Avenue du Parc to the line.September 26, 2026 – 9:10 AMThe flag drops, and the race is on after a 4km neutral section. Peloton is spread across the road with the Dutch team massed at the front.September 26, 2026 – 9:13 AMMischael Alhazmi from Saudi Arabia is the first attacker but is quickly back in the peloton.September 26, 2026 – 9:19 AMLots of chatter in the peloton as they roll by fans on the side of the road.September 26, 2026 – 9:22 AMCanada's Maggie Coles-Lyster and Alison Jackson are at the front and in the middle of the peloton, controlling things for now for their teammate, defending champion Vallieres Mill.September 26, 2026 – 9:33 AMGreece’s Argyro Milaki and Israel’s Rotem Gafinovitz attack out of a right-hand turn and get a small gap with 166km to go.Six riders try to come across to the head of the race.September 26, 2026 – 9:34 AMOne of the riders trying to come across to the duo was Canada's Alison Jackson, and the move is nullified. September 26, 2026 – 9:36 AMAnother attack by Gafinovitz with Antri Christoforou (Cyprus) jumps on, but once again, the move is shut down. Portugal's Beatriz Rosso counters solo, and there is no immediate reaction from the pelotonSeptember 26, 2026 – 9:41 AMMore riders jump from the peloton and make it across the 15-second gap to Rosso. The move includes Natalie Quinn (USA), Marte Berg Edseth (Norway), and Gergana Stoyanova (Bulgaria)September 26, 2026 – 9:44 AMTallest rider in the peloton, Teniel Campbell (Trinidad & Tobago) attacks to bridge across and that gets an immediate reaction from Alison Jackson. Jackson seems to be trying to get into a break and the peloton, led by the Dutch team, shuts that down immediately.September 26, 2026 – 9:47 AMCampbell is not giving up, as she attacks once again, and more riders jump on her wheel. But the peloton doesn't want more riders to join the four riders in the break and Campbell can't escape.September 26, 2026 – 9:49 AMFour riders made it into the break, initiated by Beatriz Rosso (Portugal) with 162 km to go, and she was joined by Natalie Quinn (USA), Marte Berg Edseth (Norway), and Gergana Stoyanova (Bulgaria). The quartet have 44 seconds with 154km to go. September 26, 2026 – 9:54 AMAnother rider tries to jump to the break but the Dutch team reels her back in. They don't want to let any other rider to join the move.September 26, 2026 – 9:59 AMThe Dutch team is lined up at the front of the peloton, with some wind impacting the riders, controlling the gap, now up 1:40 to the break.September 26, 2026 – 10:01 AMA crash takes down riders on the left side of the road. Riders going down included Adèle Normand (Canada) and Sandrine Tas (Belgium).Normand gets up quickly and is back on her bike, while Tas had to wait for her mechanic to sort out her bike.September 26, 2026 – 10:03 AMAs the peloton seems happy with the break composition, let's hear what defending Magdeleine Vallieres Mill had to say at the start this morning.“It [having the rainbow jersey] changed a lot. I mean, it's been such an honour this year to be able to wear the jersey and to be able to come back here at home and with the number one with a really good team. So yeah, it's been super special.“We're gonna try [to keep the title]. I think we have, yeah, a super strong team, so we're gonna give it a go.”September 26, 2026 – 10:06 AMAfter going to her team car, Normand stops to quickly switch one shoe that the mechanic brought to her from the car. Nicely done. With no team radios, she calmly went to the car to let them, and give time for the mechanic to get her shoe out of her bag in the car.September 26, 2026 – 10:09 AMMeanwhile, the gap to the four riders in the break is now at 2:19 with 140km to go, and the Dutch team is still controlling the front, followed by France.Tas moved through the team cars and is back in the pack.September 26, 2026 – 10:20 AMAnother crash but the riders went up and riding away very quickly with 131.7km to go.September 26, 2026 – 10:24 AMNews from the team on the ground in Montréal:Tereza Kurnická of Slovakia is actually a substitute for an injured rider, Nora Jenčušová - she's the team's soigneur and hasn't raced since 2022, except for fun on MTB.Tereza was apparently terrified of riding in a bunch this big, but she did race Worlds in 2021 as a junior so she's not a complete novice.But the countries need to enter riders to keep their qualifications for the coming years.The same will happen in the men's field tomorrow. Slovakia is putting a rider in who hasn't raced in years. September 26, 2026 – 10:26 AMBreak has 3:37 on the peloton as they head towards the Samuel-De Champlain Bridge, which could lead to more wind.Behind the Canadian team moved up to line up next to the Dutch team. Spain is also starting to move up.September 26, 2026 – 10:28 AMSeptember 26, 2026 – 10:33 AMOpened in 2015, the Samuel-De Champlain Bridge is 3.2km long, and replaced the old Champlain Bridge which was opened to traffic in 1962.The new bridge provides a multi-use pathway to pedestrians and cyclists, and three nesting boxes for peregrine falcons are installed along the bridgeThank you for coming to my Ted talk - back to racing.September 26, 2026 – 10:37 AMThe peloton is using the wide road on the bridge, happy to keep the pace steady, for now.The four riders in the break - Natalie Quinn (USA), Marte Berg Edseth (Norway), Gergana Stoyanova (Bulgaria) and Beatriz Rosso (Portugal) - have 4:26 on the peloton as they exit the bridge onto the island of Montréal.September 26, 2026 – 10:39 AMStoyanova is falling of the pace in the break while Rosso also seems to be in trouble.September 26, 2026 – 10:40 AMThe women are heading towards the 13.4km circuit, which features four key climbs. The first comes soon after the finish line with the Voie Camilien-Houde, a 1.67km ascent averaging 7.4% and reaching a maximum gradient of 10%.Next is Chemin de la Polytechnique, 790 metres at 6%, including a punishing 200-metre section at 11%. The riders then face Avenue Pagnuelo, a 534-metre climb averaging 7%, topping out around the 9km mark.The final challenge is a 600-metre drag at 4% up Avenue du Parc to the finish.It is the same circuit that the previous categories faced on Thursday and Friday. The elite women will tackle the circuit eight times.September 26, 2026 – 10:41 AMBreak now down to 2 riders: Quinn and Edseth have 4:26 with 117.8km to go.September 26, 2026 – 10:48 AMPace has increased at the front of the peloton as riders being dropped include Georgia Baker (Australia), Olympic champion Kristen Faulkner (USA)September 26, 2026 – 10:54 AMCrash. Paula Blasi (Spain) and Anna Hendersen (Great Britain) involved but get quicky back up.September 26, 2026 – 10:56 AMTwo riders in the break are: Marte Berg Edseth (Norway) and Natalie Quinn (USA) as they cross the finish line to start the circuit and see 8 laps to go.They have a lead of 3:31 . Pace is amping up in the peloton as they take on the first lap of the circuit.September 26, 2026 – 11:01 AMPeloton is racing to position themselves before the first time up Voie Camillien-HoudeSeptember 26, 2026 – 11:04 AMPoland's Kaja Rusz is one of the riders dropped, which could impact team leader Kasia Niewadoma-Phinney who is one of the top contenders. Poland started the race with 5 riders.September 26, 2026 – 11:05 AMCorrection: Faulkner was not dropped; she is still in the peloton.But Baker did pull out of the race, and that leaves the Australian team down to 3 riders.September 26, 2026 – 11:10 AMLieke Nooijen (Netherlands) is putting the hurt on the peloton on the climb, as more riders drop from the back.As we have seen in the previous races - juniors and U23s - this circuit is tough, and not many will survive at the front.September 26, 2026 – 11:16 AMStill the Dutch at the front, with Vollering only a few riders back. French and Italian team also present to prepare for the descent off the Polytechnique climb. Quite a few riders had trouble on the bottom right-hand turn onto Blvd Edouard-Montpetit in previous races.September 26, 2026 – 11:17 AMPuncture for Spain's Sara Martin, who gets assistance from her team car.As the start, leader Paula Blasi said that there was an illness going around the team.September 26, 2026 – 11:20 AMGreat Britain's Flora Perkins accelerates at the front, but the Dutch come back to the fore on the Polytechnique climb.September 26, 2026 – 11:23 AMA lot of riders down from the middle of the peloton. Riders from Sweden, Great Britain, Spain, Australia and USA involved.Defending champion Magdeleine Vallieres Mill was also involved.USA's Kate Courtney is asking for her team to get a new bike.Will provide more updates on which rider was impacted.September 26, 2026 – 11:28 AMStarting the 2nd lap, break of Quinn and Edseth see their gap reduced by half, down to 1:56.The peloton, first whittled down by the tough circuit and then decimated by the crash, was down to around 40 riders, with a large chase group of around 40 riders behind. Defending champion Vallieres, covered in road rash, is also trying to chase back with a teammate. September 26, 2026 – 11:31 AMKim LeCourt-Pienaar and Kate Courtney are in a small chasing group but they are over one minute behind the pack.Blasi, also involved in the crash, pulls out.September 26, 2026 – 11:46 AMMore riders have pulled out: Sigrid Ytterhus Haugset (Norway), Christina Schweinberger (Austria), Lauretta Hanson (Australia), and Caroline Andersson (Sweden).All the best to the riders that may be injured in that hard crash.September 26, 2026 – 11:47 AMThe gap continues to tumble for the duo off the front, down to 16 seconds as Nooijen continues to set the pace at the front of the peloton for the Dutch team. The peloton is still around 40 riders strong with 6 laps to go. A big group is chasing behind, at around 30 seconds back.September 26, 2026 – 11:50 AMEdseth is pushing ahead solo.The LeCourt and Courtney group with Evita Muzic (France), Alison Jackson, Grace Arlandson (USA) is around 1:30 from the peloton.September 26, 2026 – 11:53 AMDefending champion Vallieres Mill is still on her bike, crossing the line to start the third lap, nearly 7 minutes down with one teammate with her, Adele Normand.September 26, 2026 – 11:56 AMLast rider from the break, Edseth, is caught with 76km to go as attacks fly off the front.Behind, a chase group with Amber Kraak, Lauren Dickson, Sarah Gigante, Monica Trinca Colonel, Mavi Garcia and more are working hard to close the gap, of around 20 seconds, to the peloton.September 26, 2026 – 11:59 AMFive riders from the chase group almost connect with the peloton on the Polytechnique climb, as the attacks at the front have calmed down.The commissaires have pulled all the cars in between all the groups. September 26, 2026 – 12:04 PMAnd the 5 riders finally join the peloton with 71km to go after a long chase. Garcia put in massive pulls to make that happen.Gigante is a few metres off the back. The Australian returned to racing after over a year away, and only has one race in her legs this year.September 26, 2026 – 12:09 PMThe 47-rider peloton, still with Nooijen and the Dutch team setting the pace at the front, crosses the line and sees 5 laps to go. Germany's Franziska Koch is close to the front, behind Vollering. September 26, 2026 – 12:11 PMThe Kim LeCourt group, which has swelled to 12 riders, is 1:48 down. Canada's Olivia Baril is 2:29 back with Courtney a further 30 seconds.September 26, 2026 – 12:14 PMHuge crowd is cheering on the riders on the climbSeptember 26, 2026 – 12:18 PMGreat Britain's team leader Zoe Bäckstedt is dropped on the Camilien-Houde climb, but chases back onto the pack on the descent.The 22-year-old claimed the silver medal in the ITT earlier this week.September 26, 2026 – 12:20 PMMagdeleine Vallieres Mill waves to the crowd as she crosses the line and pulls out of the race with teammate Adele Normand. Hugs her teammate, as the right side of her body is ripped out.September 26, 2026 – 12:22 PMAttack by Spain's Mireia Benito with 61km to go. Italy's Sara Casasola and Germany's Antonia Niedermaier jump onto the move. But they are brought back.September 26, 2026 – 12:26 PMWith 60km to go, Luxembourg’s Nina Berton attacks, and gets a quick reaction from Riejanne Markus (Netherlands).The Dutch team want to control while other nations are starting to launch riders off the front, However, France has not tried anything yet, and continue to follow moves. September 26, 2026 – 12:27 PMBig move by Great Britain, Koch responds immediately.And France finally attacks with Cedrine Kerboal accelerating. She looks over her shoulder and sees the peloton on her wheel.Ana Vitória Magalhães of Brazil tries her hand but is reeled back in.September 26, 2026 – 12:31 PMOver three hours of racing done, and still 53.6 kilometres to go as the peloton starts lap 5 of 8.Koch and Niedermaier chatting, with Liane Lippert on their wheel.September 26, 2026 – 12:33 PMFrench team launches another attack as Maëva Squigan hugs the barrier, while Noemi Rüegg (Switzerland) does the work to close this down, giving a respite to the Dutch team.The Swiss team swings off, leaving the Dutch team to do the work.September 26, 2026 – 12:36 PMSquiban has 21 seconds on the peloton led by Karlijn Swinkels (Netherlands). Swinkels knows exactly what Squiban can do, and how good a descender she is, as they both race for UAE Team L’IMAD.September 26, 2026 – 12:42 PMAnother crash involving a few riders: Pfeiffer Georgi (Great Britain) and Eleonora Gasparrini (Italy).September 26, 2026 – 12:46 PMColombia's Paula Patiño attacks from the right side of the road and gets a few metres, but that move only lasted a few minutes.September 26, 2026 – 12:47 PMThe French team had someone on the side of the road with a whiteboard message for Squiban. With no race radios, it's a simple way to give information to a rider.September 26, 2026 – 12:52 PMSquiban is well known for her solo raids, as she won two Tour de France Femmes stages in 2025 by taking a flyer.The 24-year-old, who took her gloves off, has a gap of 46 seconds with three laps to go.The Dutch team is still setting the pace at the front of the peloton, down to 35 riders.September 26, 2026 – 12:54 PMPuck Pieterse ramps it up on Camilien-Houde with Vollering on her wheel, dropping riders such as Backstedt, Kopecky, Faulkner, Benito and more.September 26, 2026 – 12:56 PMAfter cracking the field, Pieterse swings off, and Vollering attacks, catches Squiban briefly and continues on solo with 38km to go.Elisa Longo-Borghini is trying to chase back. September 26, 2026 – 12:59 PMNiewadoma-Phinney, Longo Borghini in the chase group along with Pieterse. Marlen Reusser brings up another group to reinforce the chase.September 26, 2026 – 1:02 PMVollering goes into time trial mode, already with 22 seconds on the 8-rider chase group.The chase includes Italy's Elisa Longo Borghini, newly crowned time trial champion Marlen Reusser (Switzerland), Polish duo of Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney and Dominika Włodarczyk, and three French riders Maëva Squiban, Celia Gery and Juliette Berthet. And Puck Pieterse is sitting on while her team leader Vollering is off the front.September 26, 2026 – 1:06 PMReusser is doing most of the work in the chase group, but there is no sustained effort in the group other than the time trial world champion. Gap to Vollering is 22 seconds.September 26, 2026 – 1:08 PMLongo Borghini attacks from the chase group, Gery goes with her with 30km to go. The two are cooperating to bring back Vollering. September 26, 2026 – 1:10 PMReusser counters once Longo Borghini and Gery are brought back. They can see Vollering up ahead but this circuit is tricky as we saw in the previous races. September 26, 2026 – 1:12 PMVollering is on a mission but has not gained the amount of time she may have hoped for. With two laps to go, and 26.8km to go, the Tour de France Femmes champion has 20 seconds.Longo Borghini is leading the chase, flicks the elbow and Reusser comes through. September 26, 2026 – 1:16 PMOn terrain that suits her, the Camilien-Houde climb, Vollering gains a few seconds.Reusser is back at the front of the chase. Some of the riders don't have the legs, or refuse to do hard pulls to close the gap down.September 26, 2026 – 1:18 PMDominika Włodarczyk is dropped from the chase on the climb. Gery is suffering. Longo Borghini and Niewiadoma-Phinney are pulling away on the climb, and now on the hunt to catch Vollering.September 26, 2026 – 1:20 PMVollering's gap stabilized at 18 seconds.September 26, 2026 – 1:22 PMChase regroups with Longo Borghini, Niewiadoma-Phinney, Reusser and Berthet. Pieterse is still there and weirdly allowed to roll through, probably slowing things down.September 26, 2026 – 1:24 PMBig fight in the chase group to try and separate the group.Niewiadoma-Phinney attacks on Polytechnique climb, with Longo Borghini trying to stay on her wheel with 38km to go. Berthet goes deep to catch back onto the pair.September 26, 2026 – 1:26 PMPieterse and Reusser are chatting. Reusser shakes her head, one can imagine she is saying something like 'you do the work if you want to get back on'September 26, 2026 – 1:30 PMAnother big acceleration by Longo Borghini, closes the gap down to 10 seconds. Niewiadoma-Phinney takes over to shave more seconds. Vollering still has a few metres, and forcing the other two worked hard to catch her.Berthet is trying to ride herself into the wheels, while Reusser has dropped Pieterse.September 26, 2026 – 1:31 PMThe connection is made inside of 16 kilometres to go. Vollering stays at the front with Longo Borghini and Niewiadoma-Phinney on her wheel.Berthet also makes it back the group, making it four at the front. The French rider is a trade teammate of Vollering on FDJ United-Suez.September 26, 2026 – 1:34 PMMassive attack by Longo Borghini as the bell rings for the eighth and final lap. The Italian is racing her 15th road world championship.Vollering is forced to chase with Niewiadoma-Phinney on her wheel.Reusser is about 15 seconds back.September 26, 2026 – 1:37 PMLongo Borghini has 4 seconds as she climbs Camilien-Houde climb for the last time.Berthet is distanced as Niewiadoma-Phinney sits on Vollering's wheel.September 26, 2026 – 1:40 PMAnd it's back together, with 11.5km to go for Longo Borghini, Vollering and Niewiadoma-Phinney.The Dutch rider ups the pace again with 200 metres to go on the climb, dropping Longo Borghini who is paying the price for that attack,Niewiadoma-Phinney refuses to work with Vollering,Behind Berther and Reusser are together.What a race! Who will win the rainbow jersey?September 26, 2026 – 1:42 PMVollering keeps looking back at Niewiadoma-Phinney, but the Polish rider is refusing to ride.If they play games, Longo Borghini could come back, she is 11 seconds back.September 26, 2026 – 1:43 PMFinally, Niewiadoma-Phinney takes a pull at the front with 7.5km to go, but not for long. September 26, 2026 – 1:45 PMHuge crowds cheer on the riders as Longo Borghini is only 6 seconds back as the two at the front keep on looking at each other.September 26, 2026 – 1:46 PMUsing her descending skills, Niewiadoma-Phinney takes the front on the descent, going 65 km/hr.September 26, 2026 – 1:49 PMNone of the riders in the lead three have been elite road champion. The pressure is on. Vollering accelerates, trying to drop Niewiadoma-Phinney, while Longo Borghini can't quite close the gap.Niewiadoma-Phinney goes around and attacks on Polytechnique but not able to drop Vollering.September 26, 2026 – 1:52 PM2 kilometres to go as Vollering is back at the front with Niewiadoma-Phinney on her wheel.Longo Borghini is 15 seconds back and Reusser a further six seconds.September 26, 2026 – 1:53 PMNiewiadoma-Phinney takes the front under the red kite. Looks behind her, and Vollering goes through.Vollering also looks behind her to see Longo Borghini who is not giving up.September 26, 2026 – 1:56 PMNiewiadoma-Phinney launches her sprint early, sprinting side by side with Vollering fastest to the line as Niewiadoma-Phinney cramps up in the finale.Vollering finally wins the road race world title for the first time in her career.Longo Borghini uses the barriers to get close to the duo but it wasn't enough and takes bronze. Reusser is fourth and Berthet takes fifth.September 26, 2026 – 1:59 PMHere is how the top 10 shaped up after more than four hours of racingTop 10 - elite women road raceDemi Vollering (Netherlands)Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney (Poland)Elisa Longo Borghini (Italy)Marlen Reusser (Switzerland)Juliette Berthet (France)Puck Pieterse (Netherlands)Dominika Wlodarczyk (Poland)September 26, 2026 – 2:05 PMSeptember 26, 2026 – 2:09 PMWhat a race! A perfect advertisement for the Grand Prix cycliste de Montréal to add a women's race. The GP is raced on the same tough circuit around Mont-Royal.September 26, 2026 – 2:14 PMMake sure to read our post-race report on all the action while also keeping an eye on our homepage for the latest reactions and news. September 26, 2026 – 2:19 PMSeptember 26, 2026 – 2:37 PMIt is a first-world title in a row for the world's best women's cycling right nowSeptember 26, 2026 – 2:39 PMAnd that brings our penultimate live report for the World Championships in Montréal, Canada to a close. There is one more race to go: the elite men road race on Sunday. Will it be as edge-of-your-seat exciting as the elite women’s race?We’ll find out tomorrow morning starting at 9am local time.

item.title: A new twist for 30th year of Tour de Langkawi with trio of summit finishes that will have sprinters fighting to 'just survive'
item.author: simone.giuliani@futurenet.com (Simone Giuliani)
item.content:encoded: A win is never all there is at stake in any race, but somehow at Le Tour de Langkawi it's a fact that doesn't quietly tap away in the background but leaps into the spotlight with a deafening roar. For a start, the long-running Malaysian event offers a rare chance to launch a career, while for others it is a last chance to save it for those riders yet to secure a contract for 2027. Then there are the crucial points at stake in the never-ending relegation battle, and its current position near the end of the season also often makes it a farewell tour for riders who have decided, or had decided for them, that it is time to step away from the sport. Altogether, it delivers the ingredients for a heady and emotion-filled, no-holds-barred battle with the backdrop of an exotic location plus a hot and humid climate which will have the riders raising a sweat even just walking to sign in at the start of each of the eight stages from September 27 to October 4. The race, which pulls together teams from the WorldTour, ProTour, Continental ranks and national teams for a race in a region which prizes its high-level UCI race opportunities, given they are limited, will also be throwing some new elements into the mix for its 30th edition this year.Usually the sprinters are in focus for much of the event, with a decisive climbing day in the mix that is often decisive in the General Classification battle, but this year there are three summit finishes to add fire to the overall fight, with organisers pointing to the race as among the toughest editions ever. It's a welcome move for the riders who enjoy the uphill, but the sprinters and others who may not be pure climbers but perhaps thought they may be able to hang in there for one day and have a shot at the GC. "Yeah, the organisers have done a good job of removing any hope for riders like myself of having any chance at the GC with how hard they've made it this year," quipped Aaron Gate (XDS-Astana), the winner of the final stage of last year's race.Sprinter Fernando Gaviria (Caja Rural-Seguros RGA)was even more succinct when asked what he thought about the trio of climbing days: "For me it's just survive."These will be days when the fast men become allies in the autobus, looking to beat the time limit rather than enemies, getting through so they can battle once again. Those among the key sprint contenders include last year's three-time winner Matteo Malucelli (XDS-Astana) – although we are yet to see if there may be any impact in stage from a training crash on Saturday that saw him quickly subbed out of the pre-race media conference line-up as his teammate Gate was subbed in. The potential sprint competition includes the five-time Giro d'Italia and two-time Tour de France stage winner Gaviria along with Modern Adventure's Riley Pickrell, though the Canadian rider is unfortunately one teammate down even before the race has even begun. Leo Hayter posted on social media that while he made the journey to Malaysia, he then discovered that he had pericarditis, so he has had to end his season. There is only one flat stage for the sprinters – from Shah Alam to Kampar – before the climbing begins, with the introduction of the new ascent of Gunung Jerai as a shorter but steep finale for stage 2. Stage 3 then delivers an early category 2 challenge, which could well be a break launching point, though it flattens to give the fast-finishers another potential chance in Kuala Kangsar.But the next two stages, with their long and challenging ascents to the finish line, are unquestionably all about the climbers. These include new revelation speed-skater turned cyclist Jasch Lennart (Tudor), Jan Castellon (Caja Rural-Seguros RGA), Nicolas Breuillard (Total Energies), Harold Martín López (XDS-Astana) and Jonathan Caicedo (Wheeltop Rotor Chengdu), who won the 2.Pro ranked Tour of Magnificent Qinghai in July.When the Ecuadorian champion, who in 2020 won a Giro stage on top of Mount Etna, was asked if he considered himself the favourite, Caicedo said, "My goal is a top ten finish in the race. I was training very hard in Ecuador; I think I'm good for the race, I'm ready for this."Stage 4 heads into the Cameron Highlands – where overall race winner Simon Carr claimed victory in 2023 – with the road steadily ascending for more than 40km to the line. Then there is a second stage in a row that is finishing with a Hors-category climb, as the race on stage finishes in the Genting Highlands, which is an ascent that crowned Max Poole as the winner in 2024.From there, stage 6 from Pandan Indah to Rembau offers some early category 3 challenges but flattens out after the first 20km, while stage 7 from the vibrant historical location of Melaka to Batu Pahat has nothing in the way of obstacles for the sprinters but the final stage to Putrajaya delivers a category 3 climb 50km from the line which could prove a launching point for an attack as the very last chance at a tour filled with riders looking for them unfolds.*Cyclingnews attended Le Tour de Langkawi on an invitation/media package from the race that included travel and accommodation. In line with our editorial standards, our coverage is independent and was not subject to review, approval or influence by the organiser or any sponsor; no favourable coverage was promised or given in return.

item.title: 'A top three would be a hole-in-one' - McNulty, Simmons and Jorgenson give USA the best chance in decades for World Championships road race
item.author: laura.weislo@futurenet.com (Laura Weislo)
item.content:encoded: The last American rider to win on the same course in the Grand Prix de Montreal, Brandon McNulty, sees the 2026 Worlds as his country's best shot at their first elite men's title since 1993."It's the best team I think the U.S. have had," McNulty told after the time trial on Sunday. "Of course there's going to be crazy good guys from all the nations, so we have our work cut out. I think we have a good team to race super aggressively and try to do something.There's a ton of strong guys that we still don't think have ever really beaten before. So it's gonna be hard, but we have numbers to at least play our cards well."The US team have McNulty, Matteo Jorgenson and Quinn Simmons as their protected riders. After Neilson Powless withdrew from the team due to illness, according to USA Cycling, he has been replaced by Riley Sheehan, who had felt snubbed by being named as a reserve. The team also has Kevin Vermaerke, Artem Shmidt, Larry Warbasse, and Sean Quinn. McNulty, third in the GP de Montreal two weeks ago with Simmons, who finished fourth just behind, are the top contenders, together with Jorgenson, who was second overall in Tirreno-Adriatico this year, and remains one of the country's top one-day race competitors. caught up with Team USA's sports director for the elite men's race, Mike Creed, who seemed realistic about the team's chances based on the superstars they're up against - even in the absence of Tadej Pogačar, who is out because of his crash in the Vuelta a España. Isaac del Toro (Mexico), Remco Evenepoel and Wout van Aert (Belgium), and Paul Seixas (France) will be hard for the US riders to beat."[A top five] might be the best we can do, depending on who's in front," Creed tells . "We're more capable of getting a medal with multiple guys at this race than ever. That doesn't mean we should, or it'll be a failure if we don't."Matteo [Jorgenson] was there and thereabouts at Québec [eighth -ed.] and he's going to have to have better legs on the day. I'm not writing him out, but he's acknowledged that. Kevin [Vermaerke] came out of the Vuelta - he spent like the last 10 days in the breakaway, so like if he's a little cooked, it wouldn't be the most surprising thing in the world. So, if you figure that we have two guys who don't have question marks over them about their form. [It will be] clear we made a mistake if we don't have anyone in the first 15," he added before giving a golf metaphor. "Par is top 15, top 10 is like a birdie, and I think top five, top three is a hole-in-one."Obviously, it's a World [Championships], and you want to dream for the sky, but the fact is just because we are excited to be in North America and have a really good team doesn't mean that Wout and Remco aren't who they are. I love the idea of a Rocky movie triumph - I'll be the happiest guy in the world if that happens, but I don't want these guys to make moves based off of a cinematic background score."Creed was able to watch the Under-23 Women and Junior Men's races to see how the races played out on the quite arduous Montreal circuit - 13.4 kilometres long with two significant climbs and very little flat roads in between."It was similar to how I thought it was going to play out, not because I'm incredibly smart or anything, but just because the course runs a certain way. In the women's race, when [the breakaway] had two minutes, you're like, 'They're not really making any inroads,' and then when the bigger-name riders went, they got it down to 30 seconds really, really quickly," says Creed."Then, [it was the] same thing in the Junior Men's race. Unless it's a bigger group than three or four - it has to probably be like six or seven - for it to be that dangerous. Otherwise, it's just really hard to be out there by yourself or in a small group, with the fast downhills where the pack can really pick up a lot of speed - free speed, accelerating out of the turns. All these things that just really add up when you're solo or in a small group."There's no room for error - you can't get caught behind; you don't want to chase. It's not like Remco [Evenepoel] in Montreal, where he bridged to the leading five or six by himself. Even as strong as he is, he got there, then on the next lap [he paid for it]. So it's not a climb that you want to do a lot by yourself unless everyone else is already smoked."You saw in the Women's Under-23 race, the Australian girl [Felicity Wilson-Haffenden], she just was dropping bombs on people. And even then, she went just a little too early, and it kind of gassed her."In the Junior Men's race, Spain's Benjamín Noval attacked out of the bunch with 45km to go, reached the breakaway, then dropped them to go solo for almost two laps. It's the kind of scenario that a time trial world champion like Noval can pull off - and one Evenepoel can realistically do, too. How can the US team keep that from happening?"By making sure that the guys are as fresh for that attack as possible," Creed replies. "You can't make Remco not Remco. You can only just prepare yourself the best you can for that move, and then hope for a little bit of luck after that. It's not always fun to have that in a race plan; you want as little 'hope' as possible in a race plan. But ultimately, I think there's probably two other guys that eight times out of ten can follow Remco from bottom to top."That would be Seixas and Del Toro."Even then, they've got to have a fairly decent race leading into it. I think McNulty, six or seven times out of 10, is going to be able to stay with that, especially if he has a clean race. Simmons about the same, Matteo more or less the same. Because there is a drafting section in the middle of the climb. It's steeper at the bottom, then you can draft in that main part, so..."Although the team had not yet held their strategy meeting at the time of our conversation, Creed says the riders were all "on the same page and really open to playing the cards close to their chest"."I think we really want the best possible result. We all do."In order to get their best shot at a world title, Creed says the race has to be as hard as possible before the end of the 110-kilometre run-in from Brossard."I think McNulty and Quinn and Matteo are very durable riders, and the more time on the pedals for everyone, the better. It could be windy at the start and there are some open sections. I don't think it would be something where you'd get Qatar-style echelons - it won't split to like 30 [riders] and then keep it all the way to the line. But it could just cause some being on the pedals and a little bit more stress than most people would generally like for a 270km race."The run-in to the circuits is not exactly straightforward. It's got a good little bump in it; it could be crosswinds over the bridge... I might be tempting fate saying that, because maybe we'll end up on the bad side of something, but I think as much of a shit-fight of a race as possible suits us. It eliminates a lot of variables."Along with Belgium, Creed says the French team, who are fully behind Seixas, will be dictating the race."I would be surprised if France made the climb easy once," he says. "I'm sure France wants as many hard climbing kilometres as humanly possible. They probably don't want Wout to go up the road, and then have them chasing while Remco sits on. That's probably not a very enviable position. Belgium is very blessed in having a Remco because he can go with 60 km to go; he can also go with 15 km to go."The earlier an attack, the easier it will be to chase down for nations that have full squads, but it depends on who ends up in a breakaway."If Remco's not bridging to a powerhouse like a Mads Pedersen or Stefan Küng - a guy who's going to go pull-for-pull with him and just help carry him along in all the high-speed downhill and flat sections - if he goes up there with a bunch of people who are just swinging, not helping him, then maybe [he can be chased down]," says Creed."We hope the race gets chaotic, and we're able to go in some moves mid-late and not use a lot of energy - have the race come up there, and we have guys in both selections. Then we end up having numbers, and then we can play from there."It's such a delicate fine edge because you want to slip into moves rather than make the moves, and you want the people that you slip in with to be people who can carry a lot of the weight. You want some Mads Pedersen-type to go with Quinn - that's a good move. It's not necessarily a good move if Quinn and Del Toro go, because then it would be a better position to sit on, and Quinn's not going to want to sit on."Unlike in the past, Creed says riders from other countries aren't usually colluding because they share the same trade team the rest of the year."They don't do that anymore - they used to, but I think those days are gone. If you're on UAE, I think you're probably well-paid enough. That could probably happen if you had a guy who was like a straight-up domestique."You even saw last year in Kigali, Pogačar didn't wait for [Del Toro] - he kind of sat up for a second, and was like, 'Hey, you good?' And then was like, 'Oh, all right, well, I got to go, bye!' At the end of the day, they're there to win races, right?"If anything, maybe it would be like the social pressure - if you got into a two-up breakaway - of trying to pull just as hard as your teammate because you guys have a friendly rivalry. Like last year with Del Toro, maybe he should have sat on a little bit and been like, 'Bro, I'm wrecked,' but you know, you get excited and stuff. But no, that's not a problem. I mean, Quinn's teammates with Mads, you know, like, unfortunately everyone's got teammates."Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: Today on Pinstripe Alley – 9/26/26
item.author: Andrew Mearns
item.content:encoded: A good chunk of the East Coast is getting slammed by a nor’easter this weekend, so if you’re in the area, we hope you stay safe! Since this current Yankees series against the Orioles is meaningless aside from the obvious goal of staying healthy, the game originally scheduled for today was played yesterday in a straight doubleheader. They’ll take a beat today and try to play tomorrow (rookie Elmer Rodríguez is announced as the probable starter for New York in a cameo), but if it doesn’t work out, it doesn’t work out. We may just have a 161-game regular season.Anyway, the postseason looms on Tuesday! Monday’s league-wide offday is the calm before the storm, but we’ll have plenty of material coming up then so consider today our personal Pinstripe Alley calm before the storm. It’s not all quiet though, as I’m on the Rivalry Roundup, Nick is celebrating the 101st (!) birthday of the oldest living Yankee, and Michael is discussing how the Yankees’ low-minors teams fared in 2026.Game preemptively moved up to yesterday for a twin bill, so it’s an offday with Game 162 tomorrow1. Assuming Carlos Rodón is not in the Wild Card Series rotation, what do you think is the best spot to potentially deploy him out of the bullpen?2. item.title: Yankees news: Schlittler, Fried still both in play to start Game 1
item.author: Jake Devin
item.content:encoded: MLB.com | Bryan Hoch: Cam Schlittler put the finishing touches on his Cy Young season Thursday night against the Rays. It wasn’t his sharpest start, Schlittler needing 70 pitches to navigate three innings, but it put his ERA on the season at 1.95, the lowest mark by a Yankee starter since Ron Guidry posted a 1.74 ERA in his legendary 1978 season, and the third-lowest ERA in franchise history. It’s also the lowest ERA by an American League starer since Justin Verlander’s 1.75 ERA in 2022, which won the future Hall of Famer* his third Cy Young.*Incidentally, Verlander is making his final career start today in Detroit.New York Post | Dan Martin: Speaking of Schlittler, you’d expect a pitcher of his stature to be a shoe-in for Game 1 of a playoff series. However, the Yankees are considering saving him for Game 2 of the AL Wild Card Series. Max Fried could start Game 1, on extra rest, and thus also give Schlittler an extra day of rest before the Yankees embark on what they hope will be a long postseason run. Schlittler would have enough rest to start Games 2 and 5 of a potential ALDS regardless of whether he pitches Game 1 or 2 of the Wild Card Series. Is it possible the Yankees are overthinking it? Yes, admits pitching coach Matt Blake, but these are precisely the things the club’s staff is paid to overthink.Whichever way the Yankees line things up, the good news is that their excellent rotation means that they’ll have an ace-caliber talent going every night. As an aside, Andrés wrote up this debate for earlier in the week, and that’s worth a read if you haven’t checked it out yet.The Athletic | Evan Drellich and Andrew Marchand: Drellich and Marchand report on the looming lockout, and one mark to look out for next year: 60 games. Apparently, if MLB misses 60 or more games in the 2027 season, the league’s national broadcast contracts would extend an extra year, into 2029. That introduces an interesting wrinkle into the owners’ calculus when it comes to this round of labor negotiations. On the one hand, the league would still receive their negotiated dues as part of their deals with their broadcast partners. On the other, extending those deals another year means the league can’t negotiate new national deals for another year; the league is likely seeking to earn a hefty raise on their next round of national contracts. The league also wouldn’t get paid in 2029 under this scenario. SNY | John Flanigan: Ryan Weathers threw a live bullpen session yesterday, facing hitters including Giancarlo Stanton and Trent Grisham. Aaron Boone said Weathers was up to 96 mph on his fastball, though called his control a little “scattered.” According to Boone, Weathers is on track to be an option during the playoffs, but it’s unclear if the Yankees will put the left-hander on the Wild Card roster. Carlos Lagrange also threw to hitters at Yankee Stadium yesterday, though it’s unlikely he’ll be on the playoff roster soon. Boone said he isn’t in play for the Wild Card roster and Matt Blake threw cold water on the idea of him debuting in the playoffs, though it still remains a (remote) possibility that Lagrange could factor into the Yankees’ plans later in the postseason if the team advances and Lagrange’s rehab continues to go well.

item.title: Yankees pitchers strike out a whopping 17 to split Orioles doubleheader
item.author: Andrés Chávez
item.content:encoded: It wasn’t exactly a meaningful game, but the Yankees projected a much better image in the nightcap against the Baltimore Orioles and won it 6-3 after losing the first game in ugly fashion. New York’s pitchers certainly brought the strikeout stuff for this one, as Ryan Yarbrough, Will Warren, Brent Headrick, John Schreiber, and Alexander Cornielle combined to punch out 17 — tied for a team sign high among standard nine-inning efforts with a gem led by Cam Schlittler’s 13 on June 19th against the Reds.The Yankees’ record is now 93-68 with one regular season game left. If the weather holds off (no guarantees there), they have a shot at matching last year’s 94-68 record, which is frankly not bad because their best player, Aaron Judge, only suited up for 66 games. This game actually started as a pitchers’ duel, with Orioles’ starter Brandon Young and Yarbrough trading zeroes for the first 2.1 innings. The lefty departed after 49 pitches, but did not allow a run despite surrendering four hits and a walk, fanning five.The Yankees brought in Warren with one out and a runner on first, which represented a nice training scenario ahead of his expected bullpen role in the Wild Card Series.As it turned out, Warren was amazing, even though he allowed a double in that same inning that could have produced a run for Baltimore, and covered 3.2 scoreless frames while conceding a mere three hits and racking up seven strikeouts. He will finish the regular season with a nice 3.92 ERA and just over a strikeout per inning.The Yankees finally got to Young in the bottom of the fifth. After two outs, Austin Wells walked and crossed home thanks to Ryan McMahon’s RBI double.Young pitched a very solid game, completing five frames in which he conceded a single run on two hits and three walks. He whiffed six and finished the game and the season with a 3.56 ERA.The Bombers extended their lead in the bottom of the sixth against the O’s bullpen. Spencer Jones singled in Heliot Ramos, aided by a fielding error by right fielder Rece Hinds. Later in the inning, Anthony Volpe (playing shortstop with George Lombard Jr. getting a rare rest) hit an automatic double that plated Luis García Jr. and Jones to make it a 4-0 ballgame.Headrick replaced Warren in the seventh and surrendered the Orioles’ first run. With the bases loaded and one out, Leody Taveras hit a sac fly to bring in Pete Alonso. Ramos and García would hit consecutive RBI singles in the bottom of the inning, though, and the Yankees were up 6-1.Cornielle entered for his MLB debut, and was promptly greeted by a Dylan Beavers homer to right, making it a 6-2 ballgame. The rookie got into some trouble after the long ball, putting two men on base before getting the first out. He then surrendered a very long RBI double to Taveras that just missed the stands, as the O’s trimmed the Yankees lead to three runs.Cornielle then shook it off and struck out the next two hitters to end the ballgame on a high note. Ben Rice went 2-for-3 with a double, a walk, and a run scored, and McMahon went 2-for-4 with a double, a run, and an RBI. Volpe plated two, and Wells walked twice and scored once.The Yankees are supposed to wrap up their season on Sunday against the Orioles, starting at 3:20pm ET. Elmer Rodríguez has been announced as New York’s starter. However, the nor’easter that forced this doubleheader in the first place has led to some bad forecasts for Sunday, so it’s very possible that Game 162 gets nixed. We’ll find out soon enough! Stay dry out there.
